content.content:
Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node, reading it against squvoxyr, then oqotyplt; nothing runs, and no rendering is probed.

(1) Subject. A decision whose content is still a placeholder or otherwise records no commitment leaves the check with no subject to read; that absence is a finding, named as such.

(2) The entry the colour is drawn on (squvoxyr). The thing the dependent draws in a colour role is the entry that decision records as presented as a visible link: the entry is what the colour is applied to, and not another surface in place of it or in addition to it — the Content section, the section's block of paths, the content type mark, another section's value, or bare text standing for the path. The dependent also does not re-decide what that entry is or what activating it does (whether it is a link at all, its activation inputs, its outcome, what it opens), and does not make the entry's link presentation conditional on the colour: the distinction between the entry and bare text is that decision's commitment, not something the colour carries or supplies. Fail on any element that does one of these, naming it. If that decision carries no recorded commitment about such an entry, the use has nothing to be read against, and that absence is a finding.

(3) The role and its token (oqotyplt). That decision records a colour role and the VS Code theme token the role resolves to. The colour the dependent draws its entry in is that recorded colour role, drawn with the token that decision records rather than with a colour of the dependent's own: no literal colour value, no second or renamed role, no substituting another recorded role's token for the one its spec gives, and no altering of the role or of the value the spec records. Fail on any element that supplies its own colour, names a token or role the spec does not record, or otherwise changes what that decision records, naming it.

(4) No scope borrowed from the spec (oqotyplt). The spec records one element, one aspect and one state. The dependent states a colour for its own entry in the default state, does not present that spec as recording a colour for that entry or for any element beyond the one the spec names, and states no colour behaviour for a state the spec does not record — hover, selection, focus, disabled — or for anything other than the entry's own drawing. Fail on any element that attributes to that decision a commitment it does not state, naming the attribution.

(5) Non-contradiction and licence. No element of the dependent contradicts squvoxyr or oqotyplt, and no element requires a rule neither states — a different colour vocabulary or role name, a rule for resolving, normalizing or opening a path, an activation input or outcome, a stylesheet location, selector or class name, an ordering of rules, or a theme or contrast variant. Fail on any contradicting element or unlicensed rule, naming it and the prerequisite involved.

(6) Decidability. From the recorded statement alone a reviewer must be able to name an observation that would refute it without supplying a rule the dependent does not state — colour applied to text that is not the recorded link entry, an entry drawn in a colour the recorded role does not resolve to, colour presented as the thing that makes the entry a link — and if no such observation can be named from the statement, that is a finding.
content.rationale:
Both endpoints of the first edge are inline prose: squvoxyr is a commitment about how a ref-path entry is presented, and the dependent is prose about how such an entry is drawn, so that edge is the evaluation matrix's natural-to-natural cell and takes the gate form. The second edge's prerequisite is an inline visual-spec record — a fixed field grammar of element, aspect, state and value or token — which puts it on the structured layer and the dependent on the natural one; the matrix has no structured-to-natural cell beyond the default, so this edge also takes the gate form, flagged to extend the matrix. Nothing runs either way: a runnable check would have to probe the rendering of a prose child, which the strictness rule denies, and it would have to invent the rendering observable the dependent is free to state differently.

Non-violation on the surface alone would leave the two ways this decision can go wrong ungated. The first is the carrier: an appearance commitment is easy to state over the thing a reviewer has in mind and then attach to whatever renders the path, so a decision can recolour the section, the block or the type mark while saying nothing false about the link. The second is the colour's source: the link colour can be asserted as a description while the decision supplies a value of its own, overrides the recorded role, borrows another recorded role's token, or extends the spec's scope and state past the one element and one state it records. Clauses (2) to (4) therefore check where the role is applied and where the colour comes from rather than the wording; clause (5) keeps the decision from importing rules that belong to other decisions — how a path is resolved or opened, where a rule lives, what a variant is; and clause (6) keeps the commitment decidable at review time: a statement of colour from which no refuting observation can be named has settled nothing a reviewer can check.

Every clause is decidable by reading the two recorded prerequisites and the dependent; it names no endpoint-specific element, token, class, selector or wording in advance — which entry, role or state fails is the check's output, never the criterion — and states no rule its prerequisites do not, so it survives the dependent being rewritten without changing what it decides.
